narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m1'/>Both towers have five, seven and eleven, so yes, each is a multiple of the other.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But look at the blocks that only one tower has.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Sharing some primes is not enough, because the copies must also be enough.
removed_beats.on_screen: the slip's bubble shows yes, yes; the shared blocks 5, 7, 11 glow; the extra 7 and 2 in tower two glow red and the extra 11 in tower one glows red; the slip's bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>To check, put the primes in a table and count the copies in each number.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>For a multiple, the bigger number needs at least as many copies of every prime.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>For a factor, it may have at most as many copies of every prime.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the words multiple means at least as many copies and factor means at most as many copies appear

old_misconception.wrong_move: A common slip sees that both towers share five, seven and eleven and says yes, each is a multiple of the other. It ignores the extra seven and two in one tower and the extra eleven in the other.
